spot_depth.source: Fuelmaps six-venue XRP spot order-book map
methodology_and_limitations: Spot books only; no futures or perpetual depth.
Binance and Bitget are absent, including a major spot venue.
Full-depth rows are supplied by Coinbase, Bitstamp, Bitfinex and Gemini; OKX and Kraken contribute near-price depth only.
Each hourly column averages one-minute book snapshots; this is not a single synchronized raw exchange snapshot.
Hourly map can be about 65 minutes old; resting orders can be cancelled or moved.
Hidden and iceberg orders are not visible; displayed depth is not executable commitment.
No downloadable pre-recording history is available from the page.
This web-rendered observation was not captured as raw bytes in Barrot and has no Barrot SHA-256 receipt.

limitations: Observation is approximately 7.65 hours old at this run's retrieval time.
Aggregator combines overlapping exchange feeds; it is not independent of those venues' underlying derivatives data.
Liquidation figures are a lower bound because exchange real-time publication is incomplete.
Do not average with other OI providers; the run-41 provider observations differed materially in scope and level.
No raw payload or immutable Barrot receipt was captured.

interpretation.supportive_counterevidence: Fuelmaps shows bid-side displayed spot depth greater than asks across all reported bands, with 59.2% bid share within 2% and 62.3% within 10%.
interpretation.adverse_counterevidence: TradRadar's older snapshot shows declining OI, negative funding, a long-heavy account ratio and more long than short liquidations.
interpretation.timing_conflict: The TradRadar mark price is from 03:25 UTC; the Fuelmaps book is 10:00 UTC. They are not synchronized and cannot establish an intraday causal sequence.
alternative_hypotheses: Displayed bid skew may represent genuine near-price liquidity and absorption.
Displayed bid skew may be temporary/cancellable liquidity, venue composition bias or a stale hourly average.
Falling OI and negative funding may reflect leverage reduction rather than a directional bearish signal.
Long-account concentration and long liquidations may indicate crowded positioning, but not necessarily net institutional selling.
A price recovery between the two timestamps could reflect spot buying, short covering or ordinary volatility; the available observations cannot distinguish these.
